causal_chain: Conditioning the user representation on the candidate item lets the model retrieve only the subset of historical items that support that candidate.
Enforcing score stability when the top retrieved supporter is masked discourages brittle one-neighbor shortcuts and spreads evidence across multiple relevant supports.
Separately modeling supportive and contradictory historical evidence prevents broad-popularity or wrong-intent neighbors from dominating the score.
The resulting target-conditioned support-minus-contradiction score should rank held-out items better under full-sort evaluation than a static pairwise matcher.
Users with mixed tastes are poorly summarized by a single static embedding.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from increased parameter count or regularization pressure rather than from target-conditioned support/contradiction retrieval and support-drop stability.
discriminative_predictions: Compared with matched BPR_MF, the candidate should show larger ranking gains for users with longer and more diverse histories than for short-history users.
If gains are only due to parameter count, a size-matched static dual-embedding scorer without target-conditioned retrieval should match the candidate; the hypothesis predicts it will not.
Removing the contradiction channel while keeping target-conditioned support retrieval should reduce performance specifically on users whose histories span multiple item clusters.
Removing the support-drop stability term should increase reliance on a single dominant historical supporter, observable as sharper support-attention concentration and weaker ranking robustness.
expected_evidence: Ablation showing full model > support-only variant > static control or, at minimum, full model outperforming each removed-mechanism variant on qualification runs.
Attention diagnostics indicating that different candidate items for the same user activate different support subsets rather than a fixed user profile.
Per-user-slice results showing stronger benefit on high-entropy or mixed-history users.
Support-mask perturbation causing smaller score collapse for positives in the full model than in the no-stability variant.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a matched static scorer or a support-only variant matches or exceeds the full mechanism, or if target-conditioned retrieval does not vary meaningfully across candidate items for the same user, the proposed mechanism is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This proposal replaces static user-item compatibility with a target-conditioned evidence retrieval architecture that scores candidates through support and contradiction memories over each user's interacted items, plus an explicit support-drop consistency objective. That changes the core representation, interaction structure, model structure, and training procedure rather than tuning an existing operator.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that builds each user-candidate score from target-conditioned retrieval over the user's historical items, using separate support and contradiction memories plus a support-drop consistency loss, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static collaborative filtering because it can activate the right historical intent for each candidate while suppressing conflicting evidence and reducing brittle one-neighbor shortcut reliance.
implementation_requirements: Aggregate a support context and a contradiction context separately; combine them with the base user embedding in the final score.
For each training triplet (u, i+, i-), compute target-conditioned attention from candidate item to each item in the user's train history.
Implement a candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender with pairwise training.
Keep implementation within allowed dependencies only.
Learn user base embeddings, item embeddings, support-key embeddings, and contradiction-key embeddings.
Maintain train-only user history lists and a padded history matrix for batch retrieval; do not access validation/test interactions during fitting.
Provide full-sort prediction by batching candidate-item scoring with the same retrieval mechanism over the frozen catalog.
Train with BPR loss plus a support-drop consistency term that recomputes the positive score after masking the highest-attention supporter and penalizes large score drift.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use BPR_MF as the matched control under the same frozen ML-1M split, pairwise sampling regime, optimizer family, train-only fitting rule, and full-sort NDCG@10 evaluation; differences should be attributable to target-conditioned support/contradiction retrieval and support-drop consistency only.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce a Target-Conditioned Dual Evidence Retriever: for each candidate item, the model attends over a user's train-history items twice—once through a support kernel and once through a contradiction kernel—and scores the candidate using base affinity plus supportive evidence minus contradictory evidence. Add a support-drop consistency loss that masks the strongest supporter during training and penalizes excessive positive-score change.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Disable all target-conditioned history retrieval and the support-drop consistency loss, reducing the scorer to a standard static user-item dot-product BPR matrix factorization baseline with comparable embedding dimensionality and the same training/evaluation protocol.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: A single static candidate model that augments BPR_MF with target-conditioned support attention over train-history items and an explicit contradiction attention channel; qualification can first compare full model vs mechanism-off and then ablate the support-drop consistency term.
blind_projection.research_question: Can a candidate-local GeneralRecommender that scores each item by retrieving candidate-specific supportive and contradictory evidence from a user's train history outperform static pairwise collaborative filtering on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The model is feasible within the stated budget because ML-1M histories are moderate, candidate-conditioned attention can be computed over padded user histories with masked batched matrix operations, and qualification can use a compact embedding size and limited epochs without requiring external preprocessing or graph construction.
